title: Cell-free Protein Expression Using the Rapidly Growing Bacterium Vibrio natriegens
protocol: Prepare V. natriegens bacterial growth media LB-V2 as per Table 1.
Autoclave the growth media to sterilize it.
Allow the media to reach room temperature (RT).
Store excess media at RT.
Use a glycerol stock of wild type V. natriegens to inoculate 3 mL of LB-V2 media.
Grow overnight culture at 30 °C while shaking at 225 rpm.
Wash 1 mL of the overnight culture by centrifugation at 10,600 x g for 1 min.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the resulting pellet and resuspend in 1 mL of fresh LB-V2 media.
Add 1 L of fresh LB-V2 growth media to an autoclaved 4 L baffled Erlenmeyer flask with sterile cover.
Inoculate using 1 mL of washed overnight culture (1:1,000 dilution ratio).
Grow the culture at 30 °C while shaking at 225 rpm.
Monitor the culture’s OD600 using a spectrophotometer.
Harvest culture via centrifugation at 3,500 x g for 20 min at 4 °C when OD600 reaches 1.0 ± 0.2.
Place the pellet on ice.
Prepare S30 lysis buffer as per Table 1 in sterile deionized (DI) water.
Adjust pH of S30 lysis buffer to 7.7 using glacial acetic acid.
Cool S30 lysis buffer to approximately 4 °C before beginning the cell lysis procedure.
Place cell pellets on ice for 10−20 min or until completely thawed.
Resuspend all pellets resulting from the same 1 L culture using 10 mL of cold S30 lysis buffer.
Transfer suspension to a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge suspension at 3,500 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Wash the pellet a second time using 10 mL of cold S30 lysis buffer.
Place the pellet on ice.
Add 500 μL of cold S30 lysis buffer to the pellet in the 50 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellet using a wide-bore pipette tip and transfer the suspension to a 2 mL tube.
Vortex suspended pellet briefly to homogenize the cells.
Flick tubes to remove any cells on the bottom of the cap.
Place the tubes into a tube holder with caps open.
Lower sonicator tip into the suspension so that it is just under the liquid surface.
Prepare the sonication set-up using a sonicator and probe with an ⅛-inch tip diameter.
Input 20 kHz frequency and 50% amplitude into the sonicator control.
Set pulse ON time to 10 seconds and pulse OFF time to 60 seconds.
Run the pulse sonication protocol for three cycles.
If total volume of pellet suspension is > 500 μL, run the pulse sonication protocol six times.
During sonication, move the probe up and down using an adjustment knob platform.
Remove the tube from the holder and briefly vortex to re-homogenize the suspension between pulses.
Centrifuge crude cell extract at 16,000 x g for 30-45 minutes at 4°C or until lysate is free of cellular debris.
Aliquot 50 μL of supernatants into new 2 mL tubes without disturbing the pellet.
Optionally, set aside 10 μL of cell extract for post-lysis protein quantification in a separate tube.
Flash freeze crude cell extracts by placing tubes into a tube holder with a dipping string attached.
Submerge tubes into a Dewar containing liquid nitrogen and immediately place in a freezer at -80 °C until use.
Prepare working stocks of Mg-glutamate and K-glutamate in 50 mL tubes with sterile DI water at concentrations of 100 mM and 2000 mM, respectively.
Weigh out 50 g of PEG-8000 and add to the 100 mL of water in a beaker placed on a heated stir plate set to 100 °C.
Stir at 250 rpm until PEG-8000 is in solution.
Allow PEG-8000 liquid mixture to cool before transferring to 50 mL tubes.
Prepare a 1750 mM HEPES-KOH buffer by adding 20.85 g of HEPES to a 100 mL bottle.
Slowly add sterile DI water until the volume reaches 40 mL.
Vortex the bottle to dissolve the HEPES.
Use the 5 M KOH solution to adjust the pH to 8.0 and then bring the solution volume to 50 mL.
Thaw the 100 mM ATP, GTP, CTP, and UTP stocks at RT and place on ice.
Add each energy solution master mix component in accordance with Table 2 to a 15 mL tube.
Vortex the solution after each component is added.
Divide the 10x energy solution master mix into 200 μL aliquots in 2 mL tubes.
Flash freeze each aliquot and place them into the -80°C freezer until use.
Thaw each amino acid stock at room temperature.
Place thawed amino acid stocks on ice.
Use a vortex and/or thermomixer set at 37°C and 350 rpm to fully dissolve amino acids.
Add cysteine as a suspension if it does not fully dissolve.
In a 15 mL tube, add the appropriate volume of each amino acid stock to sterile DI water for an 8 mM final concentration.
Vortex the master mix solution after adding each amino acid.
Divide the 4x amino acid master mix into 200 μL aliquots in 2 mL tubes.
Flash freeze each aliquot.
Store aliquoted and flash-frozen amino acid master mix at -80°C until use.
Purify desired vector using a plasmid purification kit as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Incubate reactions for 1 h at 37 °C in a thermocycler to generate mRNA template from plasmid DNA encoding the protein of interest.
Remove 10x energy solution master mix from the -80°C freezer and thaw at room temperature (RT).
Place the thawed energy solution master mix on ice.
Remove 4x amino acid master mix aliquots from the -80°C freezer, thaw at RT, and place on ice.
Remove T7 RNA polymerase stock from the -20°C freezer and place on ice.
Remove RNase inhibitor stock from the -20°C freezer and place on ice.
Thaw DNA template at RT and place on ice.
Prepare a cell-free reaction master mix by adding amino acid master mix to a 2 ml tube on ice.
Add energy solution master mix to the cell-free reaction master mix in the 2 ml tube.
Add Mg-glutamate to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Add K-glutamate to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Add DNA template to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Add PEG-8000 to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Add T7 RNA polymerase to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Add RNase inhibitor to the cell-free reaction master mix.
Gently flick the tube after each addition to ensure mixing.
Remove V. natriegens crude cell lysate from the -80°C freezer and place on ice until thawed.
Add appropriate volume of crude cell extract to the cell-free reaction master mix as per Table 4, mixing gently by flicking or pipetting up and down.
Pipette 10 μl of the cell-free reaction master mix to the bottom of a 96- or 384-well PCR plate.
Mix the master mix by flicking the tube gently after each transfer to the PCR plate.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,000 x g for 10 s to pool any master mix that may have become stuck on the sides of the wells.
Seal the wells with a plate adhesive to prevent evaporation.
Place the PCR plate into a thermocycler set at 26°C with a heated lid set at 105°C.
Incubate the cell-free reactions for a minimum of 3 h.
Thaw mRNA template prepared in step 3.5.2 at RT and place on ice.
Perform step 4.1.1 through step 4.1.6 as previously specified for linear or plasmid DNA template using Table 4 to prepare an alternative cell-free reaction master mix for mRNA template.
Pipette 10 μL of the cell-free reaction master mix to the bottom of a black 384-well assay plate with clear glass bottoms.
Keep the assay plate on ice or work in a cold room while adding the master mix to ensure that the full kinetic profile is obtained.
Seal the wells with a clear plate adhesive to prevent evaporation.
Place the assay plate into a plate reader set at 26 °C.
Incubate the cell-free reactions for 3−6 h while monitoring the appropriate fluorescent excitation/emission wavelengths corresponding to the expressed protein.
Prepare the Mg2+ and K+ ion calibration solutions as specified in Table 5 from sterile DI water using 100 mM Mg-glutamate and 2,000 mM K-glutamate stocks.
Place calibration solutions on ice until needed.
Pipette 1 μL of the Mg-glutamate ion calibration solution into the bottom of each well in a 384-well PCR plate.
Pipette 2 μL of K-glutamate ion calibration solution onto the side of the well without touching the liquid already present in the wells.
Seal the wells with an adhesive to prevent evaporation while preparing the calibration cell-free reaction master mix.
Gently tap the 384-well plate to mix the Mg- and K-glutamate calibration solutions.
Prepare the calibration cell-free reaction master mix as specified using T7-pJL1-sfGFP plasmid DNA template in a 2 mL tube.
Add amino acid master mix to the master mix.
Add energy solution master mix to the master mix.
Add T7-pJL1-sfGFP DNA template to the master mix.
Add PEG-8000 to the master mix.
Add T7 RNA polymerase to the master mix.
Add RNase inhibitor to the master mix.
Flick the tube gently to mix after each component addition.
Pipette 7 μl of calibration cell-free reaction master mix onto the sides of the wells in a 384-well PCR plate without touching existing mixed ion calibration solution.
Reseal the wells with adhesive.
Tap the 384-well plate gently to mix the cell-free master mix with the ion calibration solution.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,000 x g for 10 s.
Place the 384-well plate into a thermocycler set at 26 °C with a heated lid set at 105 °C.
Incubate the cell-free reactions for 3 h.
Transfer the contents of each well to a black 384-well assay plate with glass bottoms using a multi-channel pipette.
Read the fluorescence of sfGFP at Ex/Em = 485 nm/528 nm using a plate reader.
Determine the ion concentration combination that yields the highest amount of protein.
